newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Central bank chief says Nigeria set for growth.
newsitem.headline: Central bank chief says Nigeria set for growth.

text.p: Nigeria's economy has emerged from economic decline and is now set for an era of growth, central bank governor Paul Ogwuma said in remarks published on Tuesday.
"I believe our dark days of economic nightmares are now behind us," he said in a speech at the University of Lagos at the weekend where he was conferred an honourary degree.
"What remains to be done is to achieve a higher rate of gross domestic product growth and per capita income and to channel the gains to the alleviation of poverty," he added.

Ogwuma, tracing Nigeria's recent economic history, said social welfare and infrastructure had been neglected in the last decade while economic policies were implemented "in fits and starts" stagnating economic growth.
This caused Nigeria's per capita national income to fall by more than 50 percent in real terms, making Nigeria "the poorest oil-producing country in the world," according to Ogwuma.
In the last three years Nigeria has achieved macro-economic stability of key measures like inflation but growth remains too slow to make an impact on the lives of ordinary people.

Ogwuma said "galloping inflation has been arrested, deficit financing has given way to A substantial fiscal surplus, the exchange rate has been stabilised after several years of volatility, the interest rates have fallen to the lowest level in recent memory, while the external reserve of the nation has hit the highest level since the post oil-boom era."
He said he was therefore "encouraged to predict that faster economic growth shall soon commence as domestic and foregin private sector investors take full advantage of the new policies."
